Geopolitical energy shocks and consumer protection under fiscal constraints
abstract: How can energy-importing governments protect fuel-dependent households during geopolitical crises without suppressing conservation incentives or making unaffordable fiscal promises? We develop conditional insurance based on pre-crisis reference fuel consumption, with transfers independent of current purchases. Under stated assumptions, fixed payments preserve the marginal pump-price signal; a strictly concave allocation problem determines how to distribute scarce assistance. A dated liquidity rule prioritizes binding infrastructure guarantees and committed low-carbon investment before discretionary relief, and identifies the conditions under which protection must be rationed or financing fails. Guarantees require verified project-specific external losses and contractual caps. French monthly fuel-price analyses for 2020–2026, a longer exploratory global VAR, and a European synthetic-control comparison of France’s September 2022 intervention illustrate implementation. The latter captures a combined public–private discount and has low-powered donor placebos; it does not isolate the causal effect of the state rebate. Externally released geopolitical energy and macro surprises provide additional exploratory transmission diagnostics; their underlying structural model is not re-estimated and French event samples remain sparse. The framework offers conditional, auditable policy rules rather than a demonstrated universal welfare ranking or unconditional sovereign solvency.

title: Translating EU renewable energy community policy under geopolitical constraint: An actor-network analysis of Cyprus
abstract: We use an actor-network concept of translation to examine how EU Renewable Energy Community (REC) policy translates into domestic practice under contested sovereignty, infrastructural isolation, and active geopolitical obstruction. Cyprus is a critical, theory-building case: the EU's last fully isolated grid, occupation of part of its territory by a third state, and Turkish obstruction of both gas exploitation and electricity interconnection make the assumptions embedded in EU policy unusually visible. Drawing on policy documents, twelve interviews and participant observation, we trace how the framework fragments as it moves from supranational design to local implementation. The evidence supports two case-derived hypotheses. The first, presupposition-mismatched translation, holds that compliance fails not for want of will or capacity but because the policy as written presupposes a context that does not exist locally, so translation fragments into competing local interpretations. The second, symmetric foreclosure, holds that where one external mechanism blocks both the domestically prioritised energy-security pathway (gas) and the EU-aligned pathway (interconnected renewable generation), competing local obligatory passage points cancel rather than converge. Their joint product is structural decoupling under material constraint, extending Bromley and Powell's means–ends decoupling to cases where the formal-substantive gap is produced by foreclosure of the prescribed means rather than by organizational choice. The argument is not that RECs cannot exist in Cyprus, but that this decarbonisation initiative receives weak domestic backing for geopolitical rather than technical reasons. We draw implications for green-transition initiatives in other peripheral, geopolitically exposed member states and for differentiated EU implementation guidance.

title: Integrated energy trading system for three types of coastal-resilient ZEBs with multiple stakeholders of novel flexibility and grid sharing resources
Modeling the electricity system in integrated assessment models - a time-series clustering approach for diverse futures
abstract: The growing role of variable renewable electricity calls for high time resolution when modeling the electricity sector. However, this can be computationally too expensive for models that combine different sectors and run over long timeframes, such as Integrated Assessment Models (IAMs). The computational burden can be reduced by, e.g., timeslicing or time-series clustering. Clustering approaches have the benefit of maintaining chronology and thus enabling electricity storage modeling; however, which hourly-level features clustering should capture for the diverse long-term scenarios calculated with IAMs have remained unclear. This paper makes a two-fold contribution to address these challenges. First, we propose an hourly-resolution electricity sub-model that links to the annual level of a suitable IAM, and uses time-series clustering to reduce the hourly dimension to a small number of representative periods. Second, we propose a new clustering approach – the multi-scenario clustering – that functions robustly across a range of future scenarios that might be calculated with an IAM. In this approach, outputs from multiple model runs covering different future scenarios are used in clustering to define representative periods. Our results show that this approach produces a clustering that works for a wide range of future scenarios nearly as accurately as a-posteriori clustering tailored for each scenario individually. Therefore, the multi-scenario clustering approach provides a robust way to save on computational burden while offering a relatively good level of accuracy in comparison to using the full, multi-year, hourly time-horizon, which would be prohibitively costly to use in IAMs.

title: Optimization and assessment of PCM-enhanced energy piles for photovoltaic-assisted geothermal harvesting
Quantum probability-driven decision framework for sustainable electric vehicle charging station placement under cognitive biases
Learning control policies from heterogeneous multi-horizon time series in battery energy management systems
abstract: This paper introduces Representation-to-Decision (R2D), an end-to-end imitation learning framework that maps heterogeneous multi-horizon time-series inputs directly to battery control decisions through modular Temporal Feature Extractors (TFEs) and a shared latent representation, without an explicit load and PV forecasting step. While accurate forecasting improves prediction quality, optimal control performance remains unguaranteed in prediction-then-optimization pipelines; standard Reinforcement Learning (RL) lacks the long-horizon temporal awareness due to short-window observations, even when forecast signals are available as additional inputs. R2D offers a different perspective: rather than forecasting first and deciding second, it learns to decide directly from raw temporal inputs, with control optimality anchored by an aging-aware Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) expert through Behavior Cloning (BC). Benchmarked against six controllers on a high-fidelity electro-thermal battery simulation across five industrial sites, R2D achieves 62--77\% of the global clairvoyant optimum, outperforms the tested Model Predictive Control (MPC) and RL benchmarks, and yields battery degradation nearly identical to its MILP teacher across all five sites. Comprehensive ablation studies over temporal backbone, model size, expert formulation, aging-cost weighting, and horizon configuration confirm that an LSTM encoder with a 15-minute single-step control horizon provides the most robust and deployment-ready configuration, and cross-site and single-factor out-of-distribution tests show that generalization to unseen profiles is profile-dependent, with policies trained on high-activity sites transferring most reliably.

title: Accurate remaining useful life prediction of lithium-ion batteries via capacity curve modeling with attention fusion learning framework
Stochastic flexibility quantification for urban integrated energy systems: Definition, modeling, and computation
Unified appliance-level flexibility modeling for residential demand response: a MILP framework considering routine disruption and thermal discomfort
Optimisation of a grid-connected electrolyser: time-ahead dispatch and energy portfolio planning
abstract: This study investigates short-term power dispatch optimisation and long-term energy capacity planning for a grid-connected water electrolysis system (WES). It explicitly accounts for key technical characteristics often overlooked in existing studies, including dynamic specific energy consumption (SEC; incorporating both stacks and balance of plant (BoP)), minimum load, ramping, and usage-based stack degradation. To enable computationally tractable optimisation without sacrificing these key technical aspects that introduce nonlinear dynamics, a two-step approach is adopted. First, nonlinear governing relationships (e.g., between input power and SEC) are derived using a detailed cell-level stack model. Second, these relationships are approximated using piecewise linearisation (PWL) with minimal error. The results show that time-ahead dispatch optimisation significantly reduces total electricity cost relative to constant operation; however, this benefit diminishes at higher required average WES utilisation due to reduced temporal flexibility (i.e., less freedom to shift production), which in turn constrains the effective use of operational flexibility (e.g., ramping). Optimal energy portfolio design is highly sensitive to yearly average WES utilisation and power purchase agreement (PPA) prices. Higher utilisation rates (URs) require increased grid-sourced firming of the power supply, whereas lower utilisation enables greater reliance on variable renewable energy (VRE), albeit with larger contracted capacities, yet remaining economically favourable. Sensitivity analysis further shows that wind PPA plays a dominant role in portfolio design, driven by its higher base cost relative to solar PPA and more consistent generation profile.

title: Machine learning-assisted bidirectional co-optimization of catalyst and operating conditions for high-yield Fischer–Tropsch fuel production
Risk-averse quantal response equilibrium based optimal bidding strategy of battery energy storage systems in the double-sided auction market
The benefits of concentrating solar hybrid systems: A unified benchmarking framework
abstract: Compact hybrid photovoltaic-concentrating solar thermal (PV-CST) systems have emerged as a promising strategy to enhance solar energy utilization by simultaneously delivering electricity and heat. Despite their potential, their assessment remains challenging due to the lack of consistent metrics capable of capturing the relative value of these distinct energy outputs. To address this gap, we introduce a unified benchmarking framework for hybrid PV-CST systems that explicitly accounts for the relative value of heat to electricity. Within this framework, we introduce the Effective Improvement Range ( EIR ), a novel metric that quantifies the resilience and competitiveness of hybrid configurations under varying heat-to-electricity value ratios. We apply this framework to three spectral-splitting hybrid architectures, named semitransparent-thermal, semitransparent-photovoltaic, and PV-mirror, each evaluated considering four photovoltaic materials (Ge, Si, GaAs, and GaP). The benefit of hybridization is assessed by benchmarking each configuration against its standalone photovoltaic and thermal counterparts, as well as against state-of-the-art reference technologies. Our analysis reveals that each hybrid architecture exhibits a well-defined optimal heat-to-electricity value ratio. Among the designs considered, GaAs-based PV-mirror systems emerge as the most robust and competitive across a broad range of conditions, offering up to 43% performance improvement over market standards. In contrast, semitransparent thermal and photovoltaic architectures yield only marginal benefits, limited to specific operating regimes and locations. These findings highlight that hybrid PV–CST systems evaluated offer modest gains over established technologies, emphasizing the need for rigorous and unified benchmarking frameworks to accurately identify and guide the development of truly competitive hybrid solar systems.

title: A reinforcement learning-based coordinated control strategy of multi-electrolyzer system for off-grid renewable energy considering safety operation
Adaptive dynamic planning method for electric vehicle charging stations considering active interaction with EV growth
abstract: Against the backdrop of rapid development in China's electric vehicle (EV) industry, the adequacy of charging infrastructure has emerged as a critical constraint. In this context, the exploration of economical and adaptable charging station (CS) planning methods is paramount. Therefore, this paper proposes an adaptive phased planning method for electric vehicle charging stations that considers transformation and expansion, based on system dynamics (SD) theory. The method explicitly accounts for the active interaction between EV ownership and planning results. Firstly, to reflect the interests of CSs, the power grid, and users, the division of phases as well as the transformation and expansion of CSs are incorporated as decision variables in the planning model. Building on this framework, an adaptive dynamic planning method is developed to minimize the combined cost of investment and queuing. Then, a predictive model for EV ownership is formulated based on SD theory to capture the active interaction between EV ownership and planning results. Finally, the immune genetic algorithm is used to solve the above programming model. The simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method can effectively address the challenges arising from the growth in EV ownership and enhance the adaptability and economy of CS planning schemes.

title: Balancing-aware observability and joint state estimation for unmanned aerial vehicle battery packs
Catalysts or constraints? The dual role of natural resources and greenfield investment amid geopolitical risk
abstract: Rapid urbanisation, industrialisation, population growth, and fast economic expansion have made emerging economies significant contributors to greenhouse gas emissions. This study assesses the impact of key economic and environmental factors on economic development, emphasising the role of green growth as an effective means to achieve sustainable development. Specifically, it examines the effect of greenfield investment (GFI), geopolitical risk (GPR), natural resources (TNR), and renewable energy consumption (GET) on green growth (GG) across 17 emerging economies from 2003 to 2022. Utilising advanced panel estimation techniques, the study concludes that GFI and GET contribute positively to green growth, whereas GPR adversely affects green growth. Similarly, the greater dependence on natural resources significantly hampers green growth, thereby confirming the presence of the ‘resource curse’ hypothesis in our analysis. Moreover, the interaction between GPR and TNR significantly dampens green growth, while the interaction between GPR and GFI further exacerbates this adverse effect. Based on these results, the study suggests that policymakers should promote greenfield investment in sustainable sectors, strengthen natural resource management through robust regulations, and mitigate geopolitical risk by diversifying international partnerships to support long-term sustainable development goals.

title: The role of aggregated EV battery storage in managing future load peaks: A New York state case study
Ligand Field Determines g-Tensor Anisotropy and Radicaloid Character of (L)RuV=O and (L)RuV=N Catalytic Intermediates
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract High-valent metal-oxo and metal-imido species mediate complex chemical transformations, yet their electronic structures remain difficult to characterize experimentally and computationally because of their short-lived nature and pronounced multiconfigurational character. The RuV (S = 1/2) complexes investigated here promote O–O bond formation in water oxidation and enable C(sp3)–H bond amination. Using multiconfigurational CASSCF/NEVPT2 calculations combined with wave function analyses, we demonstrate that g-tensor anisotropy, accessible via EPR measurements, is governed by spin–orbit coupling to low-lying doublet excited states whose energies are determined by the ligand field. Wave function analyses reveal that these transitions originate from the RuV=X (X=O, N) bonding and reflect varying degrees of RuIV-X• oxyl character. Our calculations reproduce the experimentally observed low g-tensor anisotropy of established RuV=O and RuV=N (S = 1/2) species. However, two previously reported highly anisotropic EPR signals are difficult to reconcile with a RuV assignment and can be more readily explained by proposed alternative RuIII species, which have low-lying spin–orbit-coupled excited states giving rise to the high g-tensor anisotropy. Overall results establish a quantitative relationship between the ligand field, which determines the excited-state electronic structure and radicaloid character of RuV=O and RuV=N fragments. These, in addition, manifest themselves in visualized natural orbitals and via spin–orbit selection rules, in the g-tensor anisotropy, elucidating the origins of EPR spectral features of high-valent transition-metal intermediates. Overall, our quantitative analysis establishes low g-tensor anisotropy in the EPR spectrum as a diagnostic spectroscopic signature of a high-valent RuV intermediate, should such a species be generated.

title: Arene-Perfluoroarene-Enabled Electrostatic Modulation in Organic Porous Photocatalysts for Ni/Photoredox C–N Coupling
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract How molecular connectivity can tune photoresponsive local electrostatics in porous organic photocatalysts lacking long-range order remains unclear. Here, we use arene-perfluoroarene (AP)-based constitutional design to examine this relationship in 4CzIPN-derived porous photoredox polymers. Carbazole and perfluorocarbazole units are connected through ortho-, meta-, and para-linked biphenyl bridges. Kelvin probe force microscopy reveals local light-induced contact potential difference (CPD) shifts of 27.1, 18.3, 5.0, and 4.3 mV for o-CBCP, m-CBCP, p-CBCP, and the AP-free control P(4Cz), respectively. o-CBCP also exhibits a stronger surface photovoltage response than P(4Cz) and the lowest fitted intermediate-frequency resistance under 425 nm blue LED illumination. In a catalyst-discriminating Ni/photoredox C–N coupling reaction, product yields follow the same order as the local CPD shifts. With 0.2 mg of photocatalyst on a 0.2 mmol reaction scale, o-CBCP affords the product in good yield, whereas P(4Cz) gives only trace product. These findings identify linkage geometry as a molecular handle for tuning photoresponsive local electrostatics and catalytic behavior in disordered porous polymer photocatalysts.

title: Field-calibrated surrogate prediction and uncertainty-aware decision diagnostics for multi-unit geothermal organic Rankine cycle plants
Synthesis of Medium-Sized Cyclic Ethers via Endo -Selective Pd(0)/B(C6F5)3-Catalyzed Hydroalkoxylation of Enynols and Enynediols
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Medium-sized cyclic ethers are present in many natural products and therapeutic agents. Herein, we describe a mild catalytic method for the synthesis of 6- to 8-membered oxacycles by endo-selective hydroalkoxylation of enynols and enynediols. The utility of this method is demonstrated through the total synthesis of (±)-corypsoriol D and E. Experimental and computational mechanistic studies revealed an oxidative syn-outer-sphere proton transfer mechanism, followed by a rate-determining reductive elimination via nucleophilic attack of the alkoxide on the resulting Pd-π-allyl.

title: Inverse-IMPRESSION: A Graph-Based Platform for Molecular Structure Elucidation from Experimental NMR Spectroscopic Properties
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Here, we present a platform built on our inverted graph transformer network, IMPRESSION-G2, which can accurately and rapidly reconstruct molecular bonding directly from experimental nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopic information. It comprises three interconnected stages: a one-shot model that reads in NMR parameters and uses these to predict bond connectivity between atoms; a structure correction stage that corrects the predicted structures by removing uncertain bonds and iteratively reassigning them; and noise-augmented multishot prediction, generating an ensemble of candidate structures, which are ranked to identify the best-fit structure. By integrating a range of 1H and 13C NMR data, including two-dimensional (2D) experiments such as COSY, HSQC, and HMBC, the inverse-IMPRESSION platform correctly identifies the structures of 77.8% of molecules with up to 30 heavy atoms (H, C, N, O, and F) using simulated NMR data, and 11 of 19 (58%) molecules using experimental NMR data. The experimental structures solved are representative of the complex structures in synthetic and natural products that routinely challenge chemists, assessed by high nSPS scores (greater than 40) for successfully elucidated structures and molecular weights of up to 480 Da. The inverse-IMPRESSION framework thus provides a highly effective approach for automated molecular structure elucidation by using graph-based machine learning on experimental data.

title: Fine-Tuning Universal Machine Learning Potentials Enables Efficient Computation of Li Electrode Potentials in Battery Electrolytes
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The electrode potential of Li metal is fundamental to the performance and stability of Li-metal batteries, yet its accurate prediction across diverse electrolyte chemistries remains a challenge. Standard quantum chemistry using cluster models fails to account for explicit bulk solvation, while ab initio molecular dynamics is restricted by the high computational cost of thermodynamic sampling. In this work, we present an integrated framework that combines a universal machine learning potential for electrolytes with a data-efficient fine-tuning strategy to compute Li electrode potentials. This workflow achieves ab initio level accuracy using ∼200 extra density functional theory calculations per electrolyte system. Furthermore, the identified relationship between local Li+ solvation environments and electrode potential shifts provides mechanistic insights into electrolyte-dependent redox behavior and offers guidance for rational electrolyte design.

title: Single- and few-layer materials: synthesis, structure–property relationships, integration of AI/ML, and energy storage applications
Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy for proton exchange membrane fuel cells: From implementation to application
abstract: Proton exchange membrane fuel cells play a vital role in achieving a hydrogen-powered, carbon-neutral society. Although they have been deployed in stationary and transportation applications, their limited durability and reliability still restrict large-scale commercialization. Assessing internal health states is critical to overcoming these challenges by preventing operational faults and minimizing degradation rates. However, hydrogen fuel cells are highly nonlinear, multiscale, and multiphysics systems, hindering the estimation of system health states. This review investigates a nondestructive and in situ characterization technique, electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS), to characterize the health states of hydrogen fuel cells. The variation in internal health states is directly reflected in the impedance spectrum, which can be assessed through proper interpretation. Nevertheless, developing EIS for hydrogen fuel cells is a nontrivial task. Implementing and applying EIS requires interdisciplinary studies in signal processing, control theory, and machine learning in particular cases. This review systematically discusses the implementation, interpretation, and application of EIS for hydrogen fuel cells. The onboard applicability and short measurement time are key factors in EIS implementation. Model-based and DRT-based interpretation approaches are reviewed for efficiently extracting valuable health states. Based on these methods, the applications of EIS in performance characterization, fault diagnosis, degradation analysis, and prognostics are discussed. Four perspectives regarding general, non-electrical, localized, and multiphysics-integrated EIS, are proposed to highlight and guide EIS-related studies in hydrogen fuel cells. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the deployment and application of EIS in hydrogen fuel cells and offers insights into addressing durability and reliability challenges.

title: Hierarchical electricity rationing with decomposable demand-fulfillment disparity constraints in multi-microgrid distribution systems under persistent power shortages
Distributed small-reservoir pumped-storage hydropower in Europe: a GIS screening under drawdown and karst constraints
The travelling charger problem: Energy-coupled fleet optimisation for autonomous EV charging robots
How to Engineer Biological Nanopores for Single-Molecule Capture and Discrimination
abstract: Abstract Protein-based biological nanopores have emerged as versatile tools for sequencing biopolymers, identifying molecules, and probing reactions at the single-molecule level. Many biological nanopores have been characterized, revealing the significance of nanopore size, shape, and chemical composition in molecular detection and discrimination. Advancements in understanding the nanofluidic properties of nanopores have complemented engineering approaches expanding the possible applications of nanopore technology. Through a combination of structural insights, rational design, systematic screening, and molecular dynamics simulations, researchers have developed nanopores capable of distinguishing between ions, nucleic acids, peptides, and folded proteins with remarkable specificity and sensitivity. Building upon three decades of progress, this Review highlights recent engineering innovations, discusses ongoing challenges, and explores the prospects in the field.

title: Dual-layer energy management of photovoltaic hydrogen production under limited battery capacity: An FLC–MPC framework for fluctuation mitigation
Low-carbon collaborative scheduling of industrial microgrids with electrolytic aluminum load considering electricity-carbon trading
Global sensitivity analysis of optimal capacity planning for green ammonia production under grid dependency and energy curtailment constraints
Photocatalytically Generated Nitrate Radicals Drive Decomposition of Perfluorooctanoic Acid
abstract: ABSTRACT Nitrate radicals (NO 3 •) generated in irradiated aqueous TiO 2 suspensions at acidic pH drive decomposition of perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA). The key role played by NO 3 • is demonstrated by the dependence of the reaction rate on the initial concentration of nitrate ions and by scavenging tests. The amount of nitrate ions remains constant during the process, indicating its catalytic behavior. The existence of nitrate radicals under the given conditions is here for the first time directly demonstrated by time‐resolved transient absorption spectroscopy. The process achieves ∼90% degradation of PFOA in 9 h with ca. 57% fluoride liberation. Theoretical results suggest that nitrate radicals trigger water‐mediated hydrogen atom transfer from the protonated PFOA, followed by decarboxylation and hydroxylation to the corresponding alcohol (experimentally detected), which eventually evolves to shorter‐chain intermediates. The proposed process represents the first proof of concept of the reactivity of NO 3 • with PFAS, but more importantly may be of practical relevance when coupled with the acidic regeneration of adsorbents currently used for remediation of water effluents containing PFAS.

title: The Elusive [B(ReO 4 ) 4 ] − Anion in the Non‐Centrosymmetric Crystal Structure of K[B(ReO 4 ) 4 ]
abstract: ABSTRACT The reaction of KReO 4 with B 2 O 3 in molten Re 2 O 7 results in the formation of a colorless crystalline powder of K[B(ReO 4 ) 4 ]. The single‐crystal structure determination reveals a non‐centrosymmetric structure (space group I ), containing the hitherto unknown [B(ReO 4 ) 4 ] − anion. This anion presents the first example of a monomeric anion with boron as a central atom coordinated by four perrhenate anions forming B─O─Re bonds. The compound has been further characterized by Raman spectroscopy, with additionally DFT calculations to assign the vibration modes. Moreover, the absence of inversion symmetry has been proven by second harmonic generation (SHG) measurements.

title: Layered Precursor‐Guided Growth of Nondegenerate Amorphous In 2 O 3 Approaching the Thickness Limit
abstract: ABSTRACT Oxide semiconductors are promising channel materials for ultrathin electronics. However, conventional growth methods often produce excess carriers, poor stability, and interfacial issues, limiting their electronic applications. Here, we present a layered precursor‐guided synthesis of atom‐thin amorphous indium oxide (In 2 O 3 ) by oxidizing a layered InSe precursor within a back‐end‐of‐line (BEOL)‐compatible thermal budget. The oxide thickness is precisely controlled by the number of precursor layers, enabling In 2 O 3 as thin as 0.63 nm at the physical thickness limit. By avoiding localized nucleation and island coalescence issues, the resulting In 2 O 3 exhibits atomically smooth surfaces and excellent electrostatic uniformity with potential variations below 22 meV. Capacitance‐voltage analyses confirm a carrier density of 2.8 × 10 18 cm −3 in the nondegenerate regime and a low interface trap density of 10 10 ∼10 11 cm −2 ·eV −1 . title: Thermodynamically Guided Antisite Ordering Stabilizes Cobalt‐Free Ultrahigh‐Ni Cathodes
abstract: ABSTRACT Eliminating Co from ultrahigh‐Ni layered cathodes often exacerbates Li/Ni mixing, impeding Li + transport, amplifying reaction heterogeneity, and accelerating structural degradation. Most strategies focus on minimizing the overall degree of cation mixing, whereas thermodynamic control of antisite spatial organization remains underexplored. Here, we address this central stability challenge by developing a thermodynamics‐guided defect‐engineering strategy that stabilizes spatially correlated Li/Ni antisite configurations in cobalt‐free ultrahigh‐Ni cathodes. Density functional theory screening of high‐valence dopants reveals that Te 6+ exhibits the strongest energetic preference for spatially correlated antisite configurations. This prediction guides the synthesis of LiNi 0.948 Al 0.045 Te 0.007 O 2 containing coherent local antisite‐ordered superlattice domains. These ordered domains persist after prolonged cycling, strengthen interlayer coupling, suppress H2–H3 phase separation and c ‐axis contraction, and preserve low‐barrier Li + migration pathways. Local Te–O coordination further stabilizes lattice oxygen and mitigates oxygen‐loss‐induced surface reconstruction. Consequently, the cathode delivers 185 mAh g −1 at 10 C, retains 96.7% of its initial capacity after 200 cycles at 1 C with a 4.4 V cutoff, and retains 92% of its initial capacity after 100 cycles with a 4.6 V cutoff. These findings establish the spatial organization of defects as a critical design variable for mitigating the stability‐transport trade‐off in cobalt‐free ultrahigh‐Ni layered cathodes.

title: Maleimide‐Functionalized Conjugated Polymers Enable Covalent Biotic–Abiotic Integration to Boost Microbial Electrosynthesis
abstract: ABSTRACT Integrating advanced conductive materials into microbial electrosynthesis systems is a powerful paradigm for merging abiotic performance with biotic specificity, facilitating sustainable transformation of organic waste and carbon dioxide into value‐added chemicals. The regulation of biotic‐abiotic hybrid interfaces in biohybrids is crucial for improving surface microbial abundance, enhancing electron injection, and increasing electrosynthesis production. Herein, maleimide‐functionalized conjugated polymers (p(mNDI‐gT2)) were employed to construct robust, covalent bio‐interfaces via in situ click reactions with cytochrome thiol groups of Shewanella oneidensis , resulting in a doubling of bacterial adhesion. Moreover, intimate contact and binding interactions drastically reduce interfacial resistance and boost electron injection. As a direct consequence of this optimized architecture, the system achieved a 23‐fold increase in electron transfer and a 6‐fold improvement in electrochemical reduction relative to bare S. oneidensis . Furthermore, it obviously outperformed the non‐covalent group, yielding a 2‐fold enhancement in total charge output and a 2‐fold increase in succinate yield. Molecular docking simulations and proteomic analysis collectively reveal that p(mNDI‐gT2) not only facilitates efficient charge transfer but also predominantly upregulates the expression of key respiratory and bio‐interface protein complexes. Fundamentally, this covalent biotic–abiotic interface transcends traditional bulk‐adsorption methods, shifting the paradigm from simple microbial coating to molecular‐level interface engineering.

title: A Precision‐Delivered Singlet Oxygen Generator With an Inbuilt Safety Switch for Induction of Pancreatic Beta Cell Stress and Death
abstract: ABSTRACT Type 1 diabetes (T1D) is characterized by autoimmune destruction of pancreatic beta cells, leading to insulin dependence. Preclinical models have been instrumental in advancing our understanding of the pathogenesis and treatment of T1D. Chemical agents such as streptozotocin or alloxan are widely used to induce beta cell destruction without the need for genetic alteration. However, streptozotocin and alloxan exhibit variable efficacy, can be taken up non‐specifically into other organs, and possess carcinogenic properties. As such, there is a need for more specific and less toxic models of beta cell stress. Here, we design and evaluate ROXendin668, a glucagon‐like peptide‐1 receptor (GLP1R) agonist coupled to a singlet oxygen ( 1 O 2 ) sensitizer. ROXendin668 targets pancreatic beta cells through engagement of GLP1R and potentially GCGR, followed by red light‐controlled generation of 1 O 2 . Upon illumination, ROXendin668 selectively ablates MIN6 β‐cells and primary islet β‐cells and induces localized β‐cell stress in vivo after systemic delivery. Thus, ROXendin668 represents a precise, controllable, and potentially safer alternative to existing chemical models of beta cell stress.

title: Bright Tin Halide Perovskite Quantum Dots via Organic Dication Compensatory Doping
abstract: ABSTRACT Tin halide perovskite quantum dots (THP QDs) are promising alternatives to their lead analogs for red and near‐infrared emission. However, cation vacancies cause strong p ‐doping, limiting the photoluminescence quantum yields (PLQYs) of quantum‐confined THP QDs. Low formation energies of charged cation vacancies hinder doping control through stoichiometry alone, while effective aliovalent doping strategies for extrinsic control of carrier concentrations remain lacking. Here, we establish organic dications, such as ethylenediammonium (EN), as effective electron‐donor dopants for THP QDs. Aliovalent A‐cation substitution compensates the p ‐character, enhancing the PLQY by over two orders of magnitude. CsSnI 3 ‐EN QDs ranging in size from 4 to 16 nm emit beyond 750 nm with PLQYs up to 38%. Enhancements extend to various dications and hybrid FASnI 3 QDs. The pristine, hole‐doped THP QDs exhibit a size‐dependent infrared absorption band arising from valence‐to‐valence intraband transitions, which disappears upon compensatory EN doping. X‐ray photoelectron spectroscopy reveals increased core‐level binding energies for all three perovskite constituents, consistent with a Fermi level shift of approximately 0.1 eV away from the valence band. Density functional theory calculations corroborate this finding and elucidate the defect equilibria. These results establish organic dications as donor dopants for near‐infrared emissive THP QDs.

title: Scalable Upcycling of Industrial Waste Polytetrafluoroethylene Into Porous Carbon Nanosheets by Zeolite Particle Templates for Capacitive Energy Storage
abstract: ABSTRACT Upcycling highly stable polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) waste into value‐added carbon materials is fundamentally hindered by its complete zero‐residue pyrolysis, which exclusively emits hazardous fluorocarbons rather than forming solid carbon frameworks. Herein, we present a scalable zeolite‐particle‐templated cocarbonization strategy that catalytically transforms industrial PTFE waste into hierarchical porous carbon nanosheets (PCNs) while fixing over 81% of the fluorine as recyclable NaF. Comprehensive mechanistic investigations reveal that the ZSM‐5 template electronically activates C─F bonds and lowers the defluorination barrier, driving a successive‐condensation structural evolution. The resulting PCN, featuring an ultrahigh specific surface area and hierarchical porosity, delivers exceptional dual‐mode energy storage performances. In supercapacitors, PCNs achieve a remarkable specific capacitance of 429.6 F g −1 and outstanding rate capabilities driven by reversible pseudocapacitance and ion coadsorption. Concurrently, in carbon‐based aqueous zinc‐ion batteries (CAZBs), the PCNs deliver a high specific capacity of 267.0 mAh g −1 with robust extreme‐temperature adaptability (−25°C). Validated by a continuous industrial‐scale piping and instrumentation design (PID), this strategy demonstrates high commercial viability with low energy storage costs, pioneering a waste‐to‐wealth strategy for advanced carbon materials for energy storage.

title: Dynamic Molecular Scaffold Enables Thermomechanical Stress Regulation and Adaptive Defect Healing for Stable Perovskite Solar Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT Thermally induced stress accumulation is a major origin of lattice disorder, defect evolution, and ion migration in perovskite solar cells (PSCs), limiting their long‐term operational stability. We develop a dynamic molecular scaffold strategy based on the adduct of α‐lipoic acid and N‐hydroxysuccinimide ester to mitigate thermomechanical degradation through simultaneous thermomechanical stress buffering, lattice anchoring, and adaptive defect healing. During film formation, DL‐α‐lipoic acid‐N‐hydroxysuccinimide ester (LA‐NHS) undergoes in situ polymerization to establish a crosslinked polydisulfide scaffold at grain boundaries. The dynamic scaffold accommodates thermally induced lattice expansion and contraction, dissipates accumulated stress, anchors the perovskite lattice, and continuously passivates stress‐generated defects through reversible disulfide‐bond exchange, thereby preserving lattice ordering and improving the thermal durability. Consequently, the optimized PSCs achieve a champion power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 27.19%. The devices retain 91.71% of their initial efficiency after 150 thermal cycles between 15°C and 100°C, and 85.72% after 1500 h at 85°C. The strategy is successfully translated to large‐area PSCs (25.02% for 1 cm 2 and 22.06% for 10 × 10 cm 2 ). This work establishes a dynamic molecularscaffold framework for managing thermomechanical degradation through stress buffering, lattice anchoring, and adaptive defect healing, providing a route toward efficient, durable, and scalable perovskite photovoltaics.

title: Air‐Stable Radical Additives Modulate Spin‐Dependent Recombination in High‐Efficiency Organic Solar Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT Triplet‐associated recombination remains a potential loss channel in high‐efficiency nonfullerene organic solar cells, particularly when separated charges re‐encounter to form spin‐correlated charge‐transfer or polaron‐pair states. Here, we introduce the air‐stable organic radical TTM‐1Cz as an additive to manipulate the triplet formation by the single electron–occupied doublet state characteristic of radicals. Electron paramagnetic resonance measurements confirm that the radical character of TTM‐1Cz is retained after solution processing. Grazing‐incidence wide‐angle x‐ray scattering measurements show that TTM‐1Cz and its structurally related closed‐shell analogue α HTTM‐1Cz induce comparable, modest increases in crystalline coherence, indicating a structural contribution associated with the common molecular framework. In contrast, charge‐separated‐state‐normalized transient absorption spectroscopy reveals a pronounced reduction in the late‐time triplet‐associated signal only in the TTM‐1Cz‐containing blend. Together with magneto‐photocurrent measurements and local molecular‐complex calculations, these observations are consistent with an additional, radical‐specific perturbation of spin‐dependent charge‐transfer recombination. The optimized D18:L8‐BO:TTM‐1Cz device achieves a champion power conversion efficiency of 20.63%, with a certified efficiency of 20.45%. These results reveal a design principle for radical additives in organic solar cells, in which molecular‐packing effects and spin‐active modulation of recombination act as distinct but complementary contributions.

title: Waveguided, Self‐Sensing Sheath–Core Liquid Crystal Elastomer Fiber Actuators
abstract: ABSTRACT Soft actuators capable of operating in confined and hard‐to‐access environments, while providing integrated self‐sensing capabilities, are highly desired for next‐generation robotic systems. Here we report a waveguided sheath‐core optical fiber actuator consisting of a liquid crystal elastomer core encased in a conductive sheath of carbon nanotubes/carbon black. Near‐infrared light guided through the fiber actuator drives reversible contractions of up to 38% and enables a load‐bearing capacity of up to 320 times the actuator's own weight. Arrays of these fibers enable independent optical addressing of individual actuators, allowing programmable multimodal gripping in confined environments. The conductive sheath simultaneously serves as a strain sensor, providing real‐time monitoring of actuation states via changes in resistance. By integrating photothermal actuation and self‐sensing into a single fiber architecture, this work establishes a multifunctional platform for soft robotic systems operating in spatially confined environments.

title: Coprecipitation‐Enabled Scalable Synthesis of High‐Energy Density Polyanion‐Integrated Disordered Rocksalt Cathodes for Lithium‐Ion Batteries
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Disordered rocksalt cathodes (DRX) represent a compelling platform for cobalt‐ and nickel‐free high‐energy density lithium‐ion batteries. Yet their scalable synthesis remains challenging, especially for metastable DRX chemistries that have been predominantly developed via mechanochemical routes. A prominent example is polyanion‐integrated DRX (DRXPS) cathodes, which rank among the best DRX cathodes reported to date in terms of reversible energy density, but have thus far been synthesized only mechanochemically via low‐temperature ball milling. Here we demonstrate a coprecipitation–enabled solid‐state synthesis of a DRXPS cathode, Li 1.67 Mn 1.5 P 0.17 O 4 , translating a mechanochemical route into a scalable process that is compatible with established cathode manufacturing infrastructure. The workflow programs precursor chemistry via coprecipitation of Mn 2 + with HPO 4 2 − and OH − , followed by a eutectic lithium‐salt‐assisted solid‐state reaction, enabling low‐thermal‐budget DRXPS formation (450°C, 30 min) in air. The reduced thermal budget suppresses particle coarsening and yields a mixed micro‐/nanoscale particle morphology, thereby eliminating the need for post‐synthesis particle pulverization. The resulting cathodes deliver 324 mAh g −1 (935 Wh kg −1 ), demonstrating that high‐energy density DRXPS can be realized within a manufacturing‐compatible workflow. This work establishes a direct pathway toward scalable production of metastable high‐energy density DRXPS cathodes and identifies precursor engineering as the key enabler.

title: Chemical Rounding Suppresses Morphology‐Induced Interfacial Losses in Perovskite–Silicon Tandem Solar Cells
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Surface texturing in crystalline silicon solar cells imposes a fundamental trade‐off in perovskite‐silicon tandems: micrometer‐scale pyramids enable efficient light trapping but limit the conformal deposition of thin perovskite films with sub‐micrometer thickness, whereas reduced texture heights improve compatibility at the expense of optical performance and interfacial quality of the tandem device. Here, we address this challenge by combining precisely controlled submicron texturing with an ozone‐assisted chemical rounding treatment. The resulting silicon substrates feature smoothly rounded, symmetric submicron textures that suppress micro‐terrace formation and partial epitaxy at the amorphous silicon/crystalline silicon interface, while promoting more spatially uniform optoelectronic properties in the subsequently integrated top‐cell stack. The morphology‐engineered texture yields a monolithic perovskite–silicon tandem device with a power conversion efficiency of 33.25%, demonstrating that multiscale morphological control provides a powerful pathway to simultaneously improve the optical performance and interfacial quality of tandem solar cells.

title: Crystal Integrity Suppresses Bulk Trapping in Potassium Poly(Heptazine Imide) for Selective Polyester Photoreforming
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Bulk defects in organic semiconductor photocatalysts intercept photogenerated charges before interfacial reaction, constraining activity and selectivity. Here, seeded molten‐salt recrystallization yields potassium poly(heptazine imide) (PHI‐K) nanocrystals with reduced cyano content and enhanced lattice coherence for polyester photoreforming. Density functional theory and transient absorption spectroscopy identify cyano‐derived occupied states as bulk hole traps. Defect suppression preserves observable hole‐polaron absorption and extends the average exciton‐associated absorption decay time from 69.52 to 984.72 ps, consistent with reduced trap‐assisted carrier loss. Under air mass 1.5 global (AM 1.5G) irradiation, crystalline PHI‐K photoreforms alkaline‐pretreated poly(glycolic acid) and poly(lactic acid) into glyoxylic and pyruvic acids with respective target‐product carbon yields of 95.2% and 92.5%. Corresponding H 2 evolution rates reach 42.6 and 26.0 mmol g −1 h −1 , with apparent quantum yields of 50.8% and 30.1% at 400 nm, respectively. In situ infrared spectroscopy, isotope effects, and carrier kinetics support a pathway in which holes drive two‐electron oxidation of surface‐bound α‐hydroxy species while electrons reduce protons on Pt. These findings establish crystal integrity as an organic semiconductor materials principle that couples bulk charge retention to selective bond conversion in conjugated photocatalysts.

title: Directing Hole Utilization Through Self‐Reconstructed Crystallinity Differentiation for Photoelectrochemical Water Oxidation
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Photoelectrochemical water oxidation is limited not simply by light absorption, but by inefficient hole routing and utilization at the semiconductor‐electrolyte interface, together with severe defect‐mediated recombination. Here, a self‐reconstructed crystallinity‐differentiated interface is developed to program hole utilization in photoanodes. A one‐step hydrothermal synthesis creates an interlocked architecture in which highly crystalline In 2 S 3 pyramids are coupled with a disordered mixed‐anion nanosheet domain, generating a spatially polarized reaction field for directed hole accumulation and transfer. This reconstructed interface lowers the work function, redistributes the local coordination environment around In sites, and induces a spatially heterogeneous photovoltage landscape that promotes interfacial charge separation. Mild Ar annealing further serves as a defect‐selective activation step, suppressing recombination‐active defects while preserving the beneficial interfacial polarization, thereby accelerating charge injection and oxygen evolution kinetics. The optimized photoanode reaches 8.74 mA cm −2 at 1.23 V RHE , establishing interlocked crystallinity‐differentiated architecture engineering combined with defect‐selective activation as an effective strategy for sulfide photoanodes.

title: Electrochemically Driven Phenazine Autoxidation Coupled With Supported Liquid Membrane Technology for Hydrogen Peroxide Production
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Electrosynthesis offers a direct route to utilize clean electricity to create low–emission pathways for chemical manufacturing. For direct electrosynthesis of highly active compounds such as hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ), however, the close coupling of product formation and decomposition at electrode interfaces, together with energy intensive product–electrolyte separation, leads to energy losses and limited scalability. Here, we develop an electrified supported liquid membrane platform as a scalable and practical method for H 2 O 2 production as an important model compound. In this architecture, electrons from an external power source are temporarily stored in a designed organic mediator that is subsequently autoxidized within a physically segregated supported liquid membrane domain. This structural–decoupling strategy suppresses electrode driven decomposition, simplifies product handling, and permits independent tuning of electrochemical, transport, and product formation environments within a compact, modular device constructed from inexpensive components. The platform produces high–purity aqueous H 2 O 2 with Faradaic efficiencies up to 80%. We further demonstrate direct, on–site utilization of the generated oxidizing equivalents via in situ Fenton oxidation of an organic contaminant, thereby converting intermittent renewable electricity into localized water–treatment capability. More broadly, this strategy establishes an integrated and flexible reactor design framework for multiphase, electrochemically mediated synthetic processes beyond H 2 O 2 .

title: Reprogramming Stereocontrol Through Progressive Substrate Reorganization in Artificial Triplet Photoenzymes
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Precise control of stereoselectivity remains a fundamental challenge in artificial enzymatic catalysis, particularly for artificial photoenzymes that lack evolutionary coupling between photosensitizer positioning and substrate recognition. Herein, by integrating crystallography, kinetics, molecular simulations, and protein engineering, we show that the enantioselectivity of an artificial triplet photoenzyme TPe4.0_FBpA for [2+2] cycloaddition originates from a highly organized indole substrate assembly within the photoactive cavity. Guided by these insights, progressive remodeling of substrate organization through minimal active‐site engineering reverses enantiopreference (from 99.5:0.5 e.r. to 2:98 e.r.) while preserving the sequence position of the genetically encoded photosensitizer. Structural and computational analyses further support a switch in the dominant stereocontrol mode from template‐assisted substrate organization to dispersion‐driven conformational confinement. These findings establish substrate organization as a programmable determinant of stereochemical outcome in artificial photoenzymes and provide a mechanistic framework for stereodivergent excited‐state biocatalysis.

title: Lensless Wide‐Field Microscopy: Toward Next‐Generation Chemical Bioimaging
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Lensless imaging offers a new route to substantially alleviate the shackle of space‐bandwidth‐product (SBP) on conventional optical microscopes, thus high resolution and wide field‐of‐view (FOV) can be more easily achieved simultaneously. A series of lensless imaging methods have taken their place in chemical bioimaging due to their advantages of wide FOV and low cost. This review discusses the development of sensor‐proximal contact, incoherent, holographic, and ptychographic imaging and evaluates their applications across cellular phenotyping, particle and molecular sensing, as well as tissue and in vivo imaging. Particular emphasis is placed on interfacial chemical strategies involving affinity reagents, responsive materials, luminescent reactions, and engineered probes. These approaches convert nanoscale chemical events, which cannot be directly resolved by lensless systems, into amplified and spatially resolved optical signals. By combining chemical signal transduction with large‐area imaging, lensless platforms can detect individual cells, particles, and molecular events while simultaneously capturing their temporal dynamics, spatial organization, and collective evolution. This chemistry‐centered minireview highlights future opportunities for extracting multiscale spatiotemporal information from complex chemical and biological systems.

title: Topological Carbon Quantum Rings With Near‐Unity Photoluminescence for Efficient Sky‐Blue Electroluminescence
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Carbon quantum dots (CQDs) are promising environmentally benign emitters for next‐generation optoelectronic devices, yet aggregation‐caused quenching (ACQ) fundamentally limits their solid‐state emission efficiency. Existing strategies primarily rely on surface or morphological modifications, while the role of topology in regulating exciton behavior remains largely unexplored. Here, we report a topological design strategy to suppress ACQ by constructing carbon quantum rings with a closed‐loop conjugated architecture. Guided by symmetric molecular precursors, the ring formation process is elucidated by combined mass spectrometry and density functional theory (DFT) calculations, revealing a thermodynamically driven evolution from planar oligomers to curved and ultimately closed‐loop structures. This unique topology intrinsically suppresses intermolecular π–π coupling and non‐radiative decay, while enabling exciton confinement within a rigid conjugated framework. As a result, the carbon quantum rings exhibit a near‐unity photoluminescence quantum yield of 99.5% in solution and 58.9% in solid‐state films. When integrated into electroluminescent devices, efficient sky‐blue emission is achieved with a low turn‐on voltage of 2.8 V, a maximum luminance of 1020 cd m −2 , and an external quantum efficiency of 3.4%. This work establishes topology as a fundamental design parameter for carbon‐based emitters and provides a general strategy for overcoming ACQ in sustainable optoelectronic materials.

title: Design of Giant Negative Thermal Expansion Based on a Fluorite Structure
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Negative thermal expansion (NTE) is a unique phenomenon in which materials contract upon heating, and thus, there is a strong demand for rational synthetic strategies and the design of giant NTE materials. In tetracyanoborate salts, however, the formation of interpenetrated structures suppresses structural flexibility and limits NTE behavior. Herein, we demonstrated that constructing a fluorite structure is an effective strategy for enhancing NTE through the synthesis of Ba[B(CN) 4 ] 2 with toluene as a template molecule. Density functional theory calculations predicted that Ba[B(CN) 4 ] 2 exhibited pronounced volume contraction at elevated temperature among M[B(CN) 4 ] 2 (M = Ca 2+ , Sr 2+ , and Ba 2+ ). In situ X‐ray diffraction measurements showed that Ba[B(CN) 4 ] 2 exhibited giant NTE with a volumetric thermal expansion coefficient of α v = –122.0 × 10 −6 K −1 over 620–657 K after the removal of the template molecules. Phonon calculations revealed that giant NTE in Ba[B(CN) 4 ] 2 originates from a non‐rigid unit mode with strongly negative Grüneisen parameters. These findings provide a new design principle for synthesizing open‐framework materials with precisely controlled thermal expansion properties.

title: Photo‐Controlled Tandem Polymerization Enabled by a Dinuclear Salen‐Al Catalyst for Multiblock Copolymer Synthesis
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Expanding tandem polymerization beyond two mutually compatible cycles remains a formidable challenge, largely due to the stringent specificity required by most (photo)catalysts. Here, we report a dinuclear aluminum salen complex bridged by a trithiocarbonate linker that exhibits a unique intramolecular photoinduced energy/electron transfer (PET) process with fast kinetics. This catalyst enables a bidirectional chain propagation pathway and bridges vinyl monomers PET‐RAFT polymerization with epoxides/anhydrides ring‐opening copolymerization (ROCOP), racemic lactide ring‐opening polymerization (ROP), and step‐growth polymerization between in situ generated Al–O active species and diisocyanates. Under visible‐light regulation, PET‐RAFT polymerization exhibits selective on–off switching and can proceed concurrently or in tandem with ROCOP and ROP, whereas ROP occurs only after complete consumption of the anhydride in ROCOP. Leveraging the tandem nature of these four reactions under a single catalytic regime, we achieve the unprecedented one‐pot synthesis of (ABCBA) n multiblock copolymers. This approach establishes a versatile platform for constructing complex macromolecular architectures via multiple tandem polymerizations in a single reaction vessel.

title: Solvent‐Mediated Multi‐Factor Structural Modulation for Tunable Phosphorescence in Metal–Organic Frameworks
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Independently controlling phosphorescence dynamics while preserving the intrinsic emissive state is essential for establishing mechanistically clear framework‐phosphorescence relationships and rationally developing diverse phosphorescent metal–organic frameworks (MOFs). Yet conventional ligand/metal screening typically alters the emissive center. Herein, a novel solvent‐mediated multi‐factor structural modulation strategy yields five Zn‐based MOFs with tunable dimensionalities (1D, 2D, 3D) from a single metal/ligand system, exhibiting widely tunable phosphorescence lifetimes (12.6–1045.4 ms) and quantum yields (0.2%–16.2%), while retaining broadly similar ligand‐centered green emission, allowing kinetic differences to be attributed primarily to coupled structural variations. Single‐crystal structures reveal dimensional, terminal‐ligand, and guest‐confinement variations governing supramolecular interactions and framework rigidity. Theoretical analysis links these factors to distinct excited‐state localization, while γ/β descriptors link orbital mixing to intersystem crossing and radiative decay. Among the five structures, strong hydrogen bonding and guest confinement in the guest‐containing 2D MOF afford a 1045.4 ms lifetime, whereas semi‐chelate coordination and excited‐state localization in 1D MOF may favor a 16.2% quantum yield. These color‐stable, lifetime‐tunable materials enable covert exclusive‐OR optical encoding featuring parity‐check self‐validation and single‐bit error correction. This paradigm provides new chemical insights into decoupling phosphorescence dynamics from the intrinsic emissive state, enabling mechanistic elucidation and rational construction of multiscale, tailorable phosphorescent MOF systems.

title: Janus Nanoporous Metal–Phenolic Nanosheet Membranes for Highly Efficient Osmotic Energy Harvesting
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Osmotic energy, harvested by reverse electrodialysis, is a huge and promising renewable power source. However, the implementation still remains a longstanding bottleneck due to the lack of high‐efficiency membranes with both remarkable ionic conductivity and high permselectivity. Here, we report a new membrane constructed by Janus nanoporous metal–phenolic nanosheets (Janus MPNs), which overcomes the intrinsic trade‐off between ion permeability and selectivity. The Janus MPNs prepared via a facile interface‐induced coordination assembly strategy feature an asymmetric bilayer architecture comprising a microporous domain containing ∼0.96 nm pores and a mesoporous domain containing ∼9.4 nm pores, with each domain approximately 10 nm thick. The assembled Janus MPNs membrane integrates interlayer 2D nanofluidic pathways with ordered intralayer 1D nanochannels, enabling ultrafast ion transport rates approximately 21 times those of membranes relying solely on interlamellar transport. More importantly, the intrinsic sub‐nanometer pores and abundant negative surface charges within the metal–phenolic framework enable high cation selectivity, yielding a cation transference number ( t + ) of ∼0.936. When applied in reverse electrodialysis, the Janus MPNs membrane delivers a power density of 22.1 W m −2 under a simulated sea/river salinity gradient, outperforming state‐of‐the‐art two dimensional (2D)‐material‐based membranes. This work establishes new scaffolds for membrane technology and osmotic energy harvesting.

title: A Compact Fluorogenic Peptide Tag for Bright Wash‐Free Live‐Cell Imaging
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Live‐cell fluorescence imaging offers profound insights into cellular biology, yet achieving strong fluorescence signals with minimal labeling footprint and perturbation to proteins of interest remains a persistent challenge. Here we introduce FluoP‐tag, a compact fluorogenic peptide‐tag platform for tandem‐array engineering in live cells. FluoP‐tag combines a 31‐residue peptide (∼3.4 kDa) with a cell‐permeable fluorogenic dye, FluoP580 (568 Da), rationally engineered to undergo peptide‐triggered switching from a non‐emissive spirolactam state to an emissive zwitterionic state. This compact design enables wash‐free intracellular labeling and copy‐number‐dependent signal amplification in tandem‐array formats. An 8×FluoP array produced 3.37‐fold higher brightness than HaloTag labeled with a Rhodamine X‐derived probe while remaining smaller overall (∼29.5 kDa vs. ∼33 kDa). FluoP‐tag arrays further enabled protein imaging across diverse intracellular compartments, spanning biomolecular condensates in stress granules, the nucleus, and the nucleolus, and cytoskeletal architectures resolved by live‐cell structured illumination microscopy (SIM). FluoP‐tag provides a compact fluorogenic tag‐array platform for protein labeling and imaging in living cells.

title: Unraveling the Importance of Surface Hydrogen Diffusion in Photocatalysis by Isotope Probing
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Harnessing solar energy for hydrogen generation has motivated extensive efforts to optimize photocatalysts, yet reported efficiencies remain inadequate due to insufficient mechanistic understanding. Using a well‐defined Pt/TiO 2 (110) photocatalyst, time‐resolved mass spectrometry, and isotope probing, we show that surface hydrogen diffusion can constitute a key, yet largely overlooked, determinant of photocatalytic hydrogen evolution. Employing selected methanol isotopologues, we disentangle the roles of hydrogen atoms from different precursor positions in the reaction mechanism. We find that replacing 1 H with 2 H (D) suppresses the hydrogen evolution rate, resulting from kinetic limitations by deuterium migration across the oxide surface. For CD 3 OH, we show that deuterium is removed from the surface via hydroxy‐H/D exchange, drastically decreasing the D 2 formation and bypassing the diffusion bottleneck. Our findings establish hydrogen mobility as a critical component of hydrogen evolution and highlight control of surface transport processes as a promising route toward maximizing photocatalytic performance in hydrogen‐involving reactions.

title: Demonstration of a Two‐Electron Pathway in Piezoelectric Mechanochemistry: Synthesis and Mechanical Adaptation of Polythiourethane
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Mechanochemically initiated reactions have garnered interest as an unconventional method for generating new forms of reactivity. Previous studies have focused on radical‐mediated processes or two‐electron processes mediated by a ball‐milling mechanism. In this work, we present a novel mechano‐mediated reaction that utilizes focused ultrasound and mechanical vibration to generate both one‐electron and two‐electron thiol reactions in the same reaction pot. Interestingly, we find that the final reaction product can be biased depending on the reactive partner. We employ this newly reported two‐electron reaction to create the first vibrationally driven polythiourethane (PTU) through a two‐electron mechanism, as well as its adaptive polymer composites. This research presents an eco‐friendly, vibrationally promoted approach to polymer synthesis.

title: Lanthanide Separation via Selective Precipitation Under Neutral Aqueous Conditions With a Functionalized EDTA Chelator
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT In this study, we report a precipitation‐based strategy for recycling and refining neodymium (Nd) from permanent magnet e‐waste in neutral aqueous solution using a functionalized ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid (EDTA) chelator. A hydrophobic substituent, carbostyril 124, was introduced onto the EDTA framework to yield EDTA‐cs124, which exhibited a solubility profile of the ensuing lanthanide complexes capable of differentiating the lighter and heavier lanthanides. The lighter lanthanide complexes precipitated markedly faster than the heavier ones, enabling efficient separation of Nd from a Nd/Dy/Tb mixture derived from waste hard disk drive (HDD) magnets. The recycled Nd could be refined by repeated precipitations to afford 99.3% Nd purity and 77% recovery yield. Using recyclable EDTA‐cs124 provides an operationally simple and organic‐solvent‐free approach for lanthanide separation.

title: An Alkali Amide Approach to Triphosphabenzenes
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT A new approach to triphosphabenzenes using simple and commercially available alkali amide reagents is presented. LiNMe 2 catalyzes the cyclotrimerization of triphenylmethylphosphaalkyne ( 1 ) and 1‐adamantylphosphaalkyne ( 3 ) to yield 2,4,6‐tris(triphenylmethyl)‐Dewar‐1,3,5‐triphosphabenzene ( 2 ) and 2,4,6‐tris(1‐adamantyl)‐1,3,5‐triphosphabenzene ( 4 ), respectively. The reaction is solvent dependent where non‐coordinating solvents allow the reaction to proceed catalytically. In contrast, tetrahydrofuran (THF) traps cyclic 1,3‐diphosphacyclobuten‐4‐yl ( 5 ) and λ 4 ‐triphosphabenzene anions ( 6 ) by intercepting the addition of LiNMe 2 during the cyclotrimerization of 1 . In the absence of the stabilizing effect of THF, LiNMe 2 is eliminated from 6 and the symmetric 1,3,5‐triphosphabenzene 2′ forms. By extending to other Group 1 amides, we show that KN(SiMe 3 ) 2 mediates the cyclotrimerization of 1 via a C( sp 3 )–H deprotonation of weakly acidic benzyl derivatives, allowing the synthesis and characterization of functionalized λ 4 ‐triphosphabenzene anions and λ 5 ‐triphosphabenzenes ( 9a to 9e ).
